notes.gloss: Placed beside "without being interrogated upon it"; it evidently supports the sentence that the witness does no ill in giving his reason unasked.

english.html: Rendering good and pertinent reasons, as of having haunted and frequented the said du Tilh and Martin Guerre, drunk and eaten often, since their childhood, with the one or with the other.

A witness is not credible, nor worthy of faith, who does not render a reason for his saying, a of which the Judge or the commissioner ought to interrogate him b; otherwise, if the commissioner has been so gross as not to ask it, the witness is not bound to render it c2, because he ought not to show himself eager [affectionné] to answer upon that on which he is not required or sought d. Nevertheless the witness also does no ill if he renders a reason voluntarily and of himself, without being interrogated upon it. Nay, in criminal matters (of which we treat here) the witness is bound to give a reason, even though he be not required to; otherwise his saying makes no faith f.

english.html: Upon this, it is to be noted that there were three or four kinds of witnesses who came into consideration. The first, a maternal uncle of the said du Tilh, called Carbon Barrau, and thus beyond all suspicion; inasmuch as it is in no way probable that blood, in this case, would be willing to lie so far as, without any occasion, to procure the ignominious death of its own nephew.
